name: Five-character emoji tag sequences chained to smuggle a payload
notes: Companion to owasp-mcp-1-tag-block-chained-emoji-flags.json, and the sharper of the two. That fixture uses SIX-character bodies, mirroring the design note's strawman; this one uses FIVE, which is the exact length of every real subdivision code (gbeng/gbsct/gbwls). A review showed that mattered: rewriting the carve-out as the shape rule /^[a-z]{5}$/ -- the most natural weaker implementation, not a contrived one -- left the entire guard suite green while opening a total bypass, because a chained payload is spelled in exactly that shape. The carve-out is RGI-EXACT, so these bodies are not skipped and the presence detector still fires. Note what does NOT catch this: in-place decoding recovers 'ignor' etc. with the flag base characters left between them, so no signature matches -- the presence floor is the whole defence here, which is why weakening it to a shape rule is a bypass rather than a nuisance.
